title: Paul McCartney Calls Out Beatles Movies Because Paul Mescal Is Shorter Than John Lennon Actor; He Texted Director Sam Mendes: ‘Don’t Do This!’
full_text: Oct 14, 2026 7:24am PT Paul McCartney Calls Out Beatles Movies Because Paul Mescal Is Shorter Than John Lennon Actor; He Texted Director Sam Mendes: ‘Don’t Do This!’ By Zack Sharf Plus Icon Zack Sharf Digital News Director ZSharf Latest Jessica Lange Says FX Was ‘Too F—ing Cheap’ to Pay for Cars Home From ‘American Horror Story’ Set, So ‘We Had to Drive Ourselves’ 2 days ago Ben Affleck Calls ‘Justice League’ Reshoots the ‘Low Point of My Career’: ‘It Was So Gross’ How the Studio Replaced Zack Snyder With Joss Whedon 2 days ago Amanda Seyfried Rejects Sex Scenes and Turned Down a TV Series Where ‘I’d Have to Have Sex All the Time’: I Don’t Want to Be ‘Naked With a Stranger’ 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for The Rock and Ro Paul McCartney has a bone to pick with Sam Mendes , the director of the upcoming four Beatles movies starring Paul Mescal as McCartney, Harris Dickinson as John Lennon, Joseph Quinn as George Harrison and Barry Keoghan as Ringo Starr. What’s the issue? It all comes down to how tall Mescal is compared to his co-stars. “We were all the same height!” McCartney declared on the “Good Hang” podcast, noting how movies based on the Beatles wrongly depict him as shorter than his bandmates. “We were all the same height, and Ringo was a bit smaller. And if you look at photos, we’re all the same height.” Related Stories Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount “Guess what?” McCartney added about Mescal. “He is smaller than the guy who plays John. Sam Mendes is making the film. I said, ‘Sam, I’ve got just one thing that I need to say to you. You know, Paul [Mescal is] a bit smaller.’ I don’t know how Sam’s gonna deal with it. He sent me a picture, a still from the filming they were doing, and they’re crossing the Abbey Road crossing, and the Paul character is markedly smaller. I texted him: ‘Sam! Smaller? Don’t do this! You said you wouldn’t do it.’” Popular on Variety McCartney also once expressed his frustration to Sam Taylor-Johnson, director of 2009’s “Nowhere Boy,” which starred Aaron Taylor-Johnson as a teenage John Lennon. Thomas Brodie-Sangster had a supporting role as McCartney in the biographical drama but is shorter than Taylor-Johnson. “The John character, who she later married, Aaron — he’s bigger than me in the film,” McCartney said. “My character is kind of wimpy. Smaller than John. John knocks me to the floor. And it’s like, ‘Sam, this is not true!’ Her only explanation, bless her, because she’s still a good friend, she said, ‘This is a movie, it’s not a documentary.’ And I thought, ‘Well, I don’t like that explanation.’ But I couldn’t do anything, because by now she’d made the film. There was I, little Paul. John, the great big hero, and it’s like: No! It’s not true.” Mendes is directing four Beatles movies, one centered on each of the band members. The project, officially titled “The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event,” has the backing of Sony Pictures and is currently in the middle of its year-long production. All four movies will be released theatrically in April 2028. “We want people to be able to experience them in the cinema at the same during the same period,” producer Pippa Harris recently said at the BFI London Film Festival , noting she does not expect audiences to “see all four films on the same day.” “Within the same month — you might see one a week, or you might see one weekend and two the next and one the next. However you see it, I think our hope is that people will see all four films,” she added. title: Banana Republic Debuts First Scripted Microseries, an Office Comedy Starring Jack Innanen (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 7:09am Add us as a Google Preferred Source In ’The Agency,’ Jack Innanen plays four different employees of a fictional travel agency. Courtesy of Banana Republic Maybelline. Crocs. Marc Jacobs. These are just a few of the brands that have recently turned to the microdramas format to spin a yarn while, naturally, advertising their goods. And now, Banana Republic can be added to that list. The Gap-owned brand debuted the initial episode of its first scripted microdrama on Wednesday, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The Agency stars Adults and Big Mistakes actor Jack Innanen as four different employees at an old-school, full-service travel agency called Travel & Tours that is rocked when a corporate suit (played by Innanen’s Big Mistakes costar Taylor Ortega) arrives to modernize it. Milo Tucker-Meyer plays the agency’s intern. Soapy, salacious and steamy romance stories might have popularized the microdrama format globally, but the first episode of The Agency positions the series as an office comedy with quick cuts and wink-wink lines and visuals. Innanen‘s characters in the five-episode series include a manager lacking confidence, a cocky cruise specialist, an adventure expert who deeply fears adventure and a Francophile who hasn‘t left American soil since the late ’90s. As one might expect, each of his characters are impeccably dressed in Banana Republic fits. Banana Republic chief marketing officer Meena Anvary said the brand decided to try the format in order to honor its “storytelling heritage.” Banana Republic Travel & Safari Clothing Company, as the company was initially titled, was the 1978 brainchild of a journalist and newspaper illustrator (founders Mel and Patricia Ziegler) whose early catalogs paired travel stories with apparel for sale. “We viewed this as a really interesting opportunity and way for us to hit on the nostalgia of the brand that people know and love and introduce the brand to new audiences via this TikTok series, bringing in some humor and storytelling to it as well,” Anvary said. Anvary was tightlipped about whether the brand will continue to invest in microseries or more entertainment moving forward, saying executives want to see how the audience engages with this first attempt first. But The Agency , at least, is part of a larger trend as Banana Republic’s parent company, Gap, Inc., has recently invested in building up an entertainment infrastructure amid a “fashiontainment” push. Earlier this year the company hired former Paramount exec Pam Kaufman as its chief entertainment officer and fellow Paramount alum Lourdes Arocho as head of licensing . The production company behind The Agency , Banana Republic Productions, dates back to earlier this year when the label collaborated with New York’s Explorers Club on a shortform docuseries about notable figures in science and exploration. “When we look at Gap Inc.‘s fashiontainment platform, it’s been a huge area of focus at the total company,” Anvary said. “For Banana in particular, it’s about us going back to our DNA and heritage and storytelling roots.” Entertainment is particularly valuable for marketing, Anvary added, because it helps keep a brand top of mind for consumers and encourages them to consider it when making purchasing decisions. The Agency , which has been produced especially for the TikTok audience but will be available on multiple social channels, will release episodes (and some behind-the-scenes material) weekly. Watch the series debut below. @bananarepublic Meet Travel & Tours. The last travel agency in New York City, where things have been done a certain way for a very long time. Until now. New faces, big ideas, and a staff that doesn’t exactly see eye to eye. The Agency, Episode 1 is here. ♬ original sound – Banana Republic – THR

title: NBC’s ‘Dateline’ Headed to Canada
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 7:08am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Longtime 'Dateline' correspondents Keith Morrison, Josh Mankiewicz and Andrea Canning, and the team’s senior executive producer, Liz Cole, photographed July 26 at PMC Studios in Los Angeles. Photographed by Joelle Grace Taylor NBC’s Dateline , the top-rated true crime series, is getting a Canadian spin-off series north of the border from Nov. 26. Keith Morrison, who got his start in journalism in his native Canada, will be in Toronto on Wednesday to tout the first international expansion of the Dateline franchise as part of a licensing deal with Rogers Studios. Dateline Canada on Citytv and Citytv+ will be hosted by Diana Swain, a former senior investigative correspondent for CBC News and host of The Investigators on the CBC News Network in Canada. She left Canada’s public broadcaster in 2024 after 33 years with the CBC, where Morrison in part perfected his iconic Dateline voice. After starting out in Canadian radio in the 1960s, Morrison joined the CTV Network in 1973 as a correspondent, producer and eventually a news anchor. In the early 1980s, Morrison became a co-host of the CBC Network’s The Journal flagship news and current affairs program. He joined NBC in January 1986 as co-anchor of the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. news on KNBC-TV in Los Angeles. Dateline Canada will premiere with a two-hour special revisiting the wrongful conviction of Robert Baltovich, who was jailed for the murder of then-girlfriend Elizabeth Bain after her disappearance in 1990. Baltovich spent nine years in prison until 2000, before an eventual acquittal in 2008 after prosecutors dropped all charges. The Dateline Canada t eam, having reviewed police files on the case, claims to have uncovered an unreported police investigation. The long form true crime special will feature Baltovich, a retired Toronto Police officer who worked on the case and experts as it kicks off a Citytv series about sensational Canadian crimes and their victims and suspects. title: “Ruthless, Sexual Predator”: Russell Brand Rape Allegations Detailed as Prosecution Opens Case
full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arriving at Southwark Crown Court on Oct. 14, 2026. Courtesy of Getty Russell Brand ‘s rape trial is officially underway at London’s Southwark Crown Court, with the prosecution describing the disgraced actor and comedian as a “ruthless” and “calculated” sexual predator. Eight men and four women are serving on the jury, the selection of which took place on Monday and Tuesday this week . On Wednesday, Brand was photographed arriving at the court with his wife, Laura, who was reported to have warmly smiled at him throughout the proceedings in court. Brand, best known for his roles on Big Brother’s Big Mouth and in Forgetting Sarah Marshall , is accused of three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault, with six women alleging crimes dating from 1999 to 2009. He denies all of them, telling a swarm of journalists on Wednesday morning: “I feel blessed. I feel, of course, concerned, but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody — that is my prayer.” (Since the allegations have come to light, Brand has turned to Christianity and been baptized.) Related Stories Movies 'Pop Pop,' 'Kidney' and 'Sounds of the Desert': Tallinn Sets Rebels With a Cause, Critics' Picks Programs Movies Stephen Chow's 'Shaolin Soccer' Spinoff 'Kung Fu Soccer' Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China's Summer Box Office Such was the heavy media presence at Southwark Crown Court that officials were forced to put journalists in an “overflow room” watching through video link, according to BBC News coverage . The BBC described Brand as remaining “very still” throughout Wednesday’s session, rubbing what looked like a pebble. Details of the claims against Brand were revealed by the prosecution, led by lawyer Riel Karmy-Jones. She kicked off by telling the jury that Brand was “ruthless and calculated” in his attacks against the six women, who “have never met each other, and who came forward independently of each other.” “His desire, strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious,” continued Karmy-Jones in her opening remarks. She called Brand a “sexual predator,” and cited the testimony of a former friend of his, who said Brand bragged to him that he was “a ladies man, a womaniser, and an expert pick-up artist.” According to this ex-acquaintance, Brand said he wanted to “bed 5,000 women” in his lifetime and had set himself “rules” to achieve this. The first complainant, whose claims Brand says are untrue, was said by the prosecution to have been raped by Brand. In her 20s at the time, Karmy-Jones said she was told “exactly what she needed to hear” and that he manipulated the situation to have sex with her “against her will.” This woman reportedly assumed Brand was gay and left the room to use the bathroom, telling him to make a cup of tea. When she emerged from the toilet, the prosecution said, Brand was partially undressed. “She was taken aback, she was shocked and didn’t really know what to do, and in her words, she froze a bit,” said Karmy-Jones. After the alleged rape, the prosecution says Brand was questioned by police. He said if it happened, he didn’t remember the incident. He said he did not remember the complainant’s name but “had never engaged in non-consensual activity.” The first complainant said she was “too scared to say anything” because of his celebrity status. The second complainant’s allegation of indecent assault dates back to 2001, when she was in her 30s and working at MTV. After admiring Brand’s T-shirt, the prosecution said that he offered to give the woman the item of clothing. “Make sure you give it a good wash first,” she says she told him, and offered to show Brand where the toilets were. Here, prosecutors say, he asked her to “come in” and grabbed her forearm. She began struggling and pulling back and described a “desperate, wide-eyed look on his face,” according to the BBC. Brand eventually relented and went into the toilet. A third complainant says she met Brand at a party in Soho, London in 2004. In the middle of a conversation, he lurched forward and grabbed her breasts and squeezed them with both hands, the prosecution told the jury. The woman was “shocked” and Brand had a “big, weird grin” on his face, she said. He grabbed her arm and pulled her toward the toilets. As they drove to another venue later in the evening, the prosecution says Brand pulled out his penis and told the complainant to “suck it.” Karmy-Jones said: “He simply laughed but appeared to accept her refusal.” The fourth complainant relates to an incident in 2004/2005 at Capital Radio, where Brand “grabbed” the woman’s face with both hands and pushed her up against a wall, the prosecution said. “He also grabbed her body, at her breasts, sides and buttocks — aggressively,” according to Karmy-Jones’ counsel. The complainant tried to push him off, but “he was too strong. […] He continued to kiss her on her face, and down her neck and onto her chest area, grabbing her bum and moving his mouth towards her cleavage, and grabbing her breast so hard that it was painful.” She was then able to push him away. A reminder: Brand denies all of these claims. The fifth complainant is reportedly the youngest of the women involved. She is said to have met Brand when he was performing at the Hammersmith Apollo in London in 2009. The incident began with consensual vaginal sex. “She said she did not really enjoy the experience. It felt very awkward and said it could have been anyone,” according to Karmy-Jones. Brand then raped her anally, while the woman asked him to stop, the jury was told. “She spent months and years blaming herself for what had happened, and became extremely anxious and continued to be unwell as a result,” said Karmy-Jones. Prosecutors say after this interaction that the woman received a text from Brand, to which she replied something along the lines of: “Why are you even messaging me?” He is said to have responded: “Because you’re dirty, and I wanna push you further.” The fifth complainant says told him: “I think you pushed me far enough — you treated me like an animal.” His response was immediate — “I’m sorry” — and she did not see or hear from Brand again, the jury heard. The prosecution said Brand was interviewed in relation to this offence, and provided a statement to police. “In that statement he set out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting,” the counsel informed the court. The sixth complainant accused Brand of sexual assault. She says he demanded a massage when she was working with him in 2009. When she refused, Brand was described as becoming “unhappy” and said he would not complete the task otherwise. He is alleged to have fallen to his knees “and placed his head directly into her groin area.” The woman did complain at the time in 2009 and it “went higher up the ladder,” but she felt it wasn’t taken seriously. Brand denies every single allegation from these six women. Toward the end of Wednesday’s proceedings, the jury was again told that he “provided a prepared statement setting out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting.” The trial could last up to 10 weeks. title: Avatar Entertainment Adapting Vicente Vallés Novel ‘La Caza Del Ejector’ As TV Series

The London- and L.A.-based production and management company and content financier has attached screenwriters Borja Moreno and Pablo Riquelme Cuartero to adapt the book into an eight-part TV shows. Avatar founder Larry Robinson is executive producing the project. No streamer or network attached at this stage. Hunting the Executioner follows a handsome American CIA agent who partners with a beautiful Spanish secret agent as they travel the world trying to identify and neutralize a mysterious assassin killing western spies throughout the world. Related Stories Casting Moby, Hannah Stocking & Adam Rose Set For Microdrama Slate From TikTok & Made By Us Studios News Fox Entertainment & Kevin Hart's Hartbeat Strike Microdrama Deal This is the second novel written by journalist Vallés, a veteran newscaster who anchors the evening news on Spanish broadcaster Antena 3. His previous novel Operation Kazan was once set up at Universal Television, though the story involving a Russian-backed U.S. Presidential candidate ultimately was put into turnaround. Moreno and Cuartero had been hired by Universal to it. Watch on Deadline Robinson, who spoke to Deadline in Cannes at MIPCOM said: “I am excited to work with the legendary Vicente Vallés, Pablo Riquelme Cuartero and Borja Moreno to develop this exciting book into a super premium action thriller series that could air around the world.” The news comes Avatar signed an agreement for the rights to the Katy Hogan novel Out of the Darkness , Robert Enright’s bestselling Sam Pope action book series, and Mary Dearborn’s biography of Ernest Hemingway for a TV adaptation. Moreno and Riquelme Cuartero are managed by Avatar, while Vallés’ novel is published by Editorial Espasa part of Grupo Planeta. Robinson and Avatar are repped by CAA. title: Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’
full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:41am PT Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’ UFA Fiction managing director and executive producer Nataly Kudiabor discusses the dark comedy's popularity, maintaining momentum and the elements that set it apart, including its star-studded ensemble cast By Ed Meza Plus Icon Ed Meza @edmezavar Latest Apple TV’s Hit German Series ‘Where’s Wanda?’ Returns for Season 2, Again Asking: ‘How Far Would You Go to Save Your Child?’ 34 minutes ago Going Big in Japan: International French Hit ‘Bright Minds’ Season 7 Heads to Tokyo (EXCLUSIVE) 6 hours ago Louis Malle’s ‘Elevator to the Gallows’ Set for 70th Anniversary 4K Release as Jean-Jacques Beineix’s ‘Betty Blue’ Hits Big Screen After 35 Years 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Where's Wanda? Courtesy of Apple TV “Where’s Wanda?” Apple TV ’s first German series, proved a major hit for the streamer. The show’s creative team at UFA Fiction have now raised the stakes with Season 2. Set in the town of Sundersheim, the series’ first season followed parents Carlotta (Heike Makatsch) and Dedo (Axel Stein) Klatt on their desperate search for their missing daughter (Lea Drinda), with the help of tech-savvy son Ole (Leo Simon). Obtaining gear from the darknet, they spy on their neighbors and local residents, uncovering in the process many of the town’s hidden secrets. Related Stories A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride Wanda was finally found at the end of Season 1. But, found standing over a dead body, Wanda ends up behind bars in Season 2. Popular on Variety “Where’s Wanda?” Season 2 was created, written and executive produced by Oliver Lansley, whose credits include the Anna Paquin drama “ Flack ,” alongside award-winning executive producer and UFA Fiction managing director Nataly Kudiabor (“Arthur’s Law”) and Oliver Ossege (“Helgoland 513”). The series was co-created and based on a story by Zoltan Spirandelli (“Vaya con Dios”) and is directed by Tobi Baumann (“Faking Hitler”) and Christian Ditter (“How To Be Single”). Speaking to Variety about the success of “Where’s Wanda?” Kudiabor discusses the hit show’s popularity, the challenges of maintaining momentum and an ensemble cast that boasts some of Germany’s top acting talent. Season 2 picks up at “a fantastic starting point,” Kudiabor notes. Without revealing spoilers, it’s suffice to say a major plot twist at the end of Season 1 “opened up a whole new set of possibilities.” “Wanda’s parents Carlotta and Dedo are once again desperately trying to protect their daughter, this time by proving her innocence and finding the real killer. Meanwhile, Wanda finds herself in prison, where she encounters some familiar enemies and faces threats of her own. “So, while we’re telling an entirely new story, we’re staying true to the emotional heart of the series: just how far would you go to save your child?” It was that concept that propelled Season 1 and made Apple TV’s first German-language series a solid hit. “For us, the priority was always to tell a compelling story that would connect with audiences, regardless of where they live,” Kudiabor stresses. The question of how far parents would go to save their child is a universal one, she adds. “We were delighted that Apple TV shared our belief that this was a theme with strong international appeal. “At the same time,” she adds, “it was very important to us that the show retain its distinctly German identity. This was also something our co-creators Zoltan Spirandelli and Oliver Lansley felt strongly about. Even though Sundersheim is a heightened, somewhat absurd version of a German small town, we wanted audiences to feel that this story is genuinely rooted in Germany. “I believe that authenticity is actually what helps a story travel internationally. You don’t have to make something less local to make it more universal.” Identifying the key elements that have contributed to the show’s success, Kudiabor says: “I think our secret ingredient is dark comedy. Alongside a genuinely gripping and emotionally grounded crime story, humor has always been an essential part of the DNA of the show: particularly for our writer and creator, Oliver Lansley. “Oliver has an extraordinary ability to balance real emotions and very human problems with increasingly absurd and sometimes outrageous situations. You find yourself laughing at moments when you probably shouldn’t, while still being completely invested in the characters and their struggles.” It’s precisely that balance that gives the show “its distinctive tone and sets it apart from other crime and mystery shows,” she adds. Another element that has made the show so appealing is its star-studded cast. This season Sam Riley (“Mint”), Alexandra Maria Lara (“ All Those Things We Never Said ”) and David Schütter (“ Barbarians ”) join the series. Returning cast members include Nikeata Thompson (“Späti”); Harriet Herbig-Matten (“ Maxton Hall: The World Between Us ”); Gisa Flake (“Berlin Station”); Palina Rojinski (“Welcome to Germany”); Suzanne von Borsody (“Run Lola Run”); Kostja Ullmann (“A Most Wanted Man”); Devid Striesow (“All Quiet on the Western Front”); Frederic Balonier (“Maxton Hall: The World Between Us”); Sascha Geršak (“Murder Mindfully”); Torben Liebrecht (“Altered Carbon”); Aaron Maldonado-Morales (“Sun and Concrete”); and Anton Dreger (“Two Sides of the Abyss”). “We’re incredibly fortunate to have such a brilliant ensemble from Season 1, and we’re thrilled to welcome some fantastic new actors for the second season,” Kudiabor says. “For us, it’s a huge compliment when actors of this caliber tell us they loved the first season, really connect with the scripts and are excited to become part of the show.” “Having Alexandra Maria Lara and Sam Riley — who are married in real life — playing the mysterious new neighbors of Carlotta and Dedo, portrayed so wonderfully by Heike Makatsch and Axel Stein, is a real gift. Their characters arrive in Sundersheim with a big secret of their own, adding another intriguing layer to the story. Kudiabor stresses that “bringing together such an exceptional cast, including familiar faces in unexpected roles, creates a real sense of excitement and curiosity for the audience.” Looking beyond Season 2, Kudiabor teases the possibility of future adventures. “Let’s just say that Oliver Lansley and all of us still have a few tricks up our sleeves when it comes to the future of the Klatt family. title: Netflix Lays Off Around 1,000 Employees In Largest Cuts Since 2022
full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Netflix staff were informed that the company will undergo significant layoffs Wednesday, a source confirms to The Hollywood Reporter , as the streaming giant seeks a reset amid efforts to keep its global business growing. The company is expected to cut about 6 percent of its workforce, or about 1,000 people, making it the largest staff reduction at the company since 2022. Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters announced the cuts in a memo to staff Wednesday morning. The company’s product, tech, legal and HR teams are said to have been particularly impacted. “Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the co-CEOs wrote in the memo, which was obtained by THR . “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” Ted Sarandos lamented at the Bloomberg Screentime summit on Sept. 30 that “overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster.” While the company continues to post robust profits, and remains the biggest player in subscription streaming, its viewing time has stagnated in recent months. With advertising one of the company’s growth areas, it needs to keep boosting that viewership engagement. Netflix has mostly avoided large-scale layoffs in recent years (the last major round of cuts was 2022 ), though the company has made adjustments on specific teams over time. The streaming giant is set to report its Q3 earnings next week, and the company is expected to share more information at that time. You can read the memo from Sarandos and Peters below. Team – We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams. Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful. For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors. We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment – and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do. Ted and Greg More to come. THR

title: TikTok Inks Second Major Microdrama Deal, Partners With Made By Us Studios
full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hannah Stocking, who will appear in the TikTok-Made By Us Studios coproduction ‘Player,’ attends the 97th Annual Oscars at Dolby Theatre in 2025. Photo by Monica Schipper/Getty Images TikTok is deepening its commitment to the microdrama format with a new deal aimed at producing vertical stories starring creators. The company has inked an agreement with Made By Us Studios, the production arm of major creator management company Made By All, to co-produce creator-led vertical series for TikTok and its microdrama app PineDrama. It’s the social media company’s second major microdrama deal after it announced a partnership with Issa Rae’s Hoorae Media to co-develop microseries in April. Mady By All, the management company behind Made By Us Studios, represents creators including Dhar Mann (who is already making his own microdramas with Fox and Holywater), One Battle After Another actor Teyana Taylor and YouTuber Adam Waheed. Made By Us Studios is led by former Range Partner Tanya Cohen as well as Made By All founder Leanne Perice and Made By Us president of production Nic Stanich. The deal was announced at MIPCOM, where TikTok unveiled the first two projects in the slate. Player is a romantic revenge thriller starring and co-executive produced by creator Hannah Stocking and additionally produced by Jonas Barnes. The series was written by Arun Blair-Mangat and Chela Reyna and directed by Louiza Zouzias. The Knock is described as a “genre microseries” (no word yet as to the precise genre) starring actor and content creator Adam Rose and actor Zaria Simone ( Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin ). It was created and directed by R.H. Stavis and is executive produced by Spooky Pictures (Watcher) alongside the musician Moby’s Little Walnut Productions. Moby also composed the series’ music. “Micro-series are pioneering a new language of storytelling,” TikTok’s global head of entertainment and micro-series Dawn Yang said in a statement about the deal. “We’re thrilled to partner with Made By Us on a slate that puts creators at the center, alongside established producers and industry talent, to tell stories designed for the feed from the start. This is an exciting step forward in our continued investment in the next generation of premium vertical storytelling on TikTok and PineDrama.” Made By Us Studios co-CEO Tanya Cohen said in a statement that vertical series are “the next evolution” for creators. “The opportunity isn’t to make smaller versions of television — it’s to build an entirely new premium storytelling language around the way audiences actually consume entertainment today,” Cohen added. “TikTok understands that behavior at a global scale, and together we have the opportunity to build franchises with creators who arrive with audience, community and cultural relevance already built in.” TikTok’s deal with Hoorae Media started big earlier in the year with Screen Time , a hit microdrama about a terrible double date. The series, starring Xavier Avila, Jasmine Luv, Eric C. Lynch and Brittney Jefferson, has earned nearly 580 million views globally since it premiered in April. THR

Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters unveiled the move in a memo to employees Wednesday, a copy of which was obtained by Deadline. The share price of the giant streamer has dropped more than 40% over the past year as Wall Street has increasingly scrutinized its viewer engagement, which increased only 2% over the first half of the year to 97 billion hours viewed. Sarandos addressed the topic of growth earlier this month at a Bloomberg conference. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” he said. The company’s unsuccessful bid for Warner Bros. studio and streaming assets also spooked Wall Street a bit as investors took it as as sign that the company felt it needed a major deal to continue to grow, a notion Netflix’s top executives have dismissed. Additionally, the streamer has gone through one of its longest draughts without a breakout new series that has captured the zeitgeist the way shows like Stranger Things, Squid Game, Bridgerton, Queen’s Gambit, Wednesday, Baby Reindeer, and, most recently Adolescence, did. (It recently found success with its latest Harlan Coben adaptation, I Will Find You , which landed on the Most Popular English series list.) Netflix also is coming off a rare third-place finish at the Emmys behind rivals Apple TV and HBO. Interest in Netflix’s existing series is showing signs of waning too, with many returning series posting season-to-season viewership declines. The streamer has been shifting strategy by leaning into live events, including sports — including the upcoming NFL Thanksgiving Eve and Christmas Day games and the Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua boxing match — podcasts and creator-driven content. Netflix also has been increasing theatrical distribution, with its upcoming movies The Misadventures of Cliff Booth, La Bola Negra and Possible Love all getting theatrical release before hitting the platform. title: Ventana Sur Proyecta 2026: A Powerhouse New Generation Lineup Backed by Some of Latin America’s Finest Producers
full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:09am PT Ventana Sur Proyecta 2026: A Powerhouse New Generation Lineup Backed by Some of Latin America’s Finest Producers Natalia Oreiro, Maeve Jinkings are attached to star in projects; producers include Rei Pictures, Piano, Tarea Fina, Luxbox and Cannes Un Certain Regard winner Simón Mesa Soto By John Hopewell , Emiliano de Pablos Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Rabbits' Courtesy of Ocúltimo Packed to its entirety by first and second-time directors, the 12 projects at this year’s Ventana Sur Proyecta co-production forum delivers a new generation snapshot backed by some of Latin America’s finest producers which delivers a searing portrait of the contemporary realities. In key casting Brazil’s Maeve Jinkings, renowned for her pivotal role in Walter Salles’ Oscar-winning “I’m Still Here,” is set to star in “Cabildo 71.” Natalia Oreiro (“Yosi, the Regretful Spy”) in “The Other Mountain.” Related Stories David Ellison's 'Day One’ Skydance Press Conference: Studio Lot Dibs, Trump Ties and Everything Else We Learned A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. Of project confirmed Tuesday by the San Sebastián Oil. Festival, which partners on Proyecta with Cannes Festival’s Marché du Film and Ventana Sur, “Give Me Shelter” marks one of the latest projects from Rei Pictures . Based in Argentina, Mexico and Spain, it is behind Lucrecia Martel’s Venice Selected “Our Land,” Argentine Oscar submission “Kill the Jockey” and Cannes Un Certain Regard winner “The Settlers” of just recent films. Popular on Variety “Give Me Shelter” will mark Nicolás Pérez Veiga’s feature debut after an prize-laden adversing career, including seven Cannes Lions, an International Emmy nomination for “Out There” and directing “Ringo, Glory and Death.” Set up at Cannes Critics’ Week Next Step workshop, “The Absence” is produced by Julio Chavezmontes’ famed Piano, a Mexico City-based producer and co-producer on movies from Apichatpong Weerasethakul, Ruben Östlund, Lucrecia Martel and Leos Carax. “Rabbits” marks the first new Colombian director title from Colombia-based Ocúltimo, co-founded by Simón Mesa Soto , director of acclaimed “A Poet,” a Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize. Ocúltimo aims “to become a platform for new generations of Colombian filmmakers with bold, director-driven films,” Mesa Soto told Variety . “Los Mejores Días” is set up at Juan Pablo Miller’s Tarea Fina , a bastion of Argentine arthouse cinema, behind such standouts as Cannes Camera d’Or winner Las acacias,” “Incident Light” and “Sleepwalkers.” Boarded by France’s Luxbox Spain’s Amore Cine, Ventana Sur Proyecta Co-Production Forum Title “Portrait Huaco” weighs as the second feature from Melina León, whose “Song Without a Name” (“Canción sin nombre”) world premiered at the 2019 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight. A closer look at the 12 film projects at this year’s Proyecta lineup: “ The Absence,” (“La Ausencia,” Jorge Sistos Moreno, Mexico) The feature debut of Sistos Moreno, whose “The Darkness was selected for Cannes Critics’ Week in 2022. In 18th century Morelia, a mestizo woman, the lady of an estate, invokes an ancestral deity in search for a for her husband’s syphilis, passed on to her. “This film speaks to a wound that remains open even today: racism, and the inability to accept ourselves and our heritage because of the forces and paradigms imposed upon us,” says Sistos Moreno. “ Cabildo 71,” (Victoria “Pitoka” Pena, Uruguay, Brazil, Argentina, Spain) A sophomore outing for Victoria “Pitoka” Pena, whose debut feature, “Delia”, won the Silver Biznaga for Best Director at the Málaga Film Festival, “Cabildo 71” is based on real-life events about the women imprisoned in Cabildo — a prison-convent run by the nuns of the Good Shepherd. An intimate take on the biggest women’s jail break in history. Boarded by Una Presencia (Argentina) and Vitrine Filmes (Brazil/Spain), lead produced by Monarca Films of Uruguay and co-producer Boulevard Filmes, Brazil. “ Dirty Face” (“Cara sucia,” Ignacio Acconcia, Spain) Acconcia draws on a decade working with people with intellectual disabilities for his fiction feature debut. Led by Ayhe Productions alongside Kabiria Films and Barcelona-based Contraria Media, the drama follows a Black teenager with vitiligo who finds acceptance while performing community service at a disability care home. The producers are also behind the upcoming “March 14th,” winner of the Berlinale Co-Production Market’s VFF Talent Highlight Award. Ayhe’s David Aymerich says the film aims to bring underrepresented communities to the screen. ‘Dirty Face’ Courtesy of Ayhe Productions “ Give Me Shelter,” (“Un Lugar Seguro,” Nicolás Pérez Veiga, Argentina, Mexico) “A true facts-based thriller, set just days before Argentina’s 1976 military coup, “a story of resilience and courage that almost nobody knows,” says Pérez Veiga. When his father is kidnapped by a paramilitary task force days before the coup, doctor Gustavo Vaca Narvaja returns to his family and decides to risk everything on a desperate escape. “There’s only one problem: they are twenty six, and none can be left behind.” ‘Give Me Shelter’ Courtesy of Rei Pictures “ Isabel Hernández” (Giorgio Giampà, Italy-Mexico) Italy’s Zoe Films, behind Venice competition entry “A Bit of Light,” leads Giampà’s feature debut alongside LaDoc and Mexico’s Fiasco and Madrefoca. Set in Guatemala, the drama follows a young agronomist investigating her long-absent father amid the migration crisis. With established Italian arthouse distributor Teodora Film on board, the project participated in TorinoFilmLab’s FeatureLab 2026. “I was immediately drawn to the depth and complexity of its characters and its careful exploration of how trauma translates across generations,” says Fiasco’s Elena Fortes. ‘Isabel Hernández’ Courtesy of Zoe Films “ Los Mejores Días,” (Maria Zanetti, Argentina) The second feature from María Zanetti, a 2025 Argentina AMPAS best first feature for debut “Alemania.” Set over three timelines and straddling Argentina and Spain, a potentially powerful portrait of young love and an enduring passion, despite a darker side, an “exploration of love with no adornment nor emphases,” says Zanetti. “ The Other Mountain” (“La otra montaña,” Horacio Reyes Páez, Uruguay-Argentina) Natalia Oreiro (“Wakolda”) is attached to star in a new take on the 1972 Andes plane crash, told from the perspective of a mother awaiting news of her missing son. Reyes Páez, her real-life grandson, calls it “the intimate, invisible battle of a mother, far from the snow and the wreckage.” Uruguay’s U Films and Sueño Cine produce alongside Argentina’s FAM Contenidos. ‘The Other Mountain’ Courtesy of U Films “ The Place and the Hope,” (“El lugar y la esperanza,” Ariagna Fajardo Nuviola, Cuba-France) Nuviola revisits the impact of a community filmmaking initiative launched 30 years ago in her native Sierra Maestra. Produced by Julio Raúl Vega Garcés’ Torrente Films, the feature documentary draws on family archives to explore cinema’s power to preserve collective memory. Backed by Cuba’s Film Promotion Fund, it won a Eurodoc special mention at Montreal’s RIDM Forum. ‘The Place and the Hope’ Courtesy of Torrente Films “ Portrait Huaco,” (“Huaco Retrato,” Melina León, Peru, France, Spain) An awaited adaptation of Peruvian author Gabriela Wiener’s autobiographical novel “Portrait Huaco.” Gabriela returns to Lima after her father dies. Back home, she discovers a book by her great-great-grandfather, Austrian explorer Charles Wiener. Her search into the family past becomes a reckoning with the lingering legacies of colonialism, internalized racism and abandonment. Produced by Peru’s Mano de Obra Cine, led by Melissa Cordero, and La Vida Misma Films, both behind “Song Without a Name.” “ Rabbits,” (“Conejos,” Sara Nanclares, Colombia, Chile, Germany, France) A powerful high-caliber Latin-America-Europe co-production that revisits a social experiment in birth control carried out in Colombia for over 30 years. “With a sharp script and a witty, outspoken protagonist who refuses to be defined by her circumstances, the film challenges conventional views of teenage pregnancy, bringing to light the desires and contradictions that lie beneath it,” says Nanclares. “ Salamanca,” (Juan Sebastian Torales, Argentina, France) The second feature from Torales whose “Almamula,” a coming-of-age drama , rooted in the legends and folklore of the Argentine countryside, played Berlín’s 2023 Generation 14Plus. Set up at Lorena Quevedo Argentina’s Twin Latin Films (“Venezia”), who co-produced Torales’ debut. “ Unfit Mother,” (“Mala madre,” Manuela Espiñeira, Chile) Chilean outfit Pinda Producciones, behind Berlinale players “Skin in Spring” and “The Nature of Invisible Things,” teams with Espiñeira’s MoveShot on her feature debut. Actress and co-scribe Nicole Rubio stars as a progressive politician whose baby dies after she accidentally leaves him in her car, triggering a devastating personal and public reckoning. “The Movie Teller” actress Sara Becker co-stars. It explores how a woman is judged “not only for what happened, but for the way she has worked, loved and mothered,” Espiñeira says. ‘Unfit Mother’ Courtesy of Pinda Producciones HBO Max to Revamp Harry Potter Film Rewatch Podcast Into Companion Series for New TV Show (EXCLUSIVE) Tom Hanks, Ta-Nehisi Coates and More Join Barack Obama’s ‘A Great Book’ Podcast at Audible Fox News Expands Podcasts With All-Female ‘the Girls’ Ethan Hawke Stars in Supernatural Horror Podcast ‘Midnight Radio’: ‘There’s an Intimacy to the Audio-Only Medium’ Marvel Launches ‘Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday Official Podcast’ Ahead of Movie’s December Debut ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With ‘Woman in the Woods’ Loading comments...

title: Snoop Dogg’s Daughter Cori Broadus Debuts Character in Animated Series ‘Doggyland’ — Fulfilling a Childhood Dream (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All October 14, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cori Broadus Mason Sexton Snoop Dogg ‘s daughter Cori Broadus has landed a role in Doggyland , the 3D animated children’s series co-created by her father, fulfilling a childhood dream. This marks the animated debut for Broadus, who plays Maxine, a confident, sassy labradoodle, in the series, which was co-created by Snoop Dogg, Emmy-nominated producer and creator Claude Brooks and Grammy-winning artist and producer October London. Doggyland also marks the beginning of a dream come true for the actress, who has harbored ambitions of becoming part of the world of children’s animation for two decades. As a youngster, she auditioned for the animated series The Backyardigans , but didn’t land the part. Now, she now only is voicing a character but also helped create her. Related Stories Music Tupac Murder Trial: Duane "Keffe D" Davis Sentenced 40 Years to Life in Prison TV Lucian Piane, Former 'RuPaul's Drag Race' Music Producer, Dies at 46 Broadus was hands-on throughout the character development process alongside Brooks, helping shape Maxine’s personality, look and spirit. The 27-year-old describes the character as “an extension of her inner child” — bold, playful, expressive and unapologetically herself. Maxine makes her first appearance in the music video for “You’re Enough,” the title track from Doggyland ’s latest full-length album. “I’m so excited to be part of Doggyland and bring Maxine to life,” Broadus said. “I love that she’s confident, a little sassy, and encourages kids to be themselves. ‘You’re Enough’ is such a special message because I want every kid to know they’re already perfect just being who they are.” Doggyland features a cast of dogs who sing, rap and dance to fun and educational songs that promote social-emotional and cognitive development in young children. Since its inception in 2022, Doggyland has produced a variety of educational songs about affirmations, letters, numbers, colors, animals, good habits and accepting others. The series focuses on delivering positive messages through music and storytelling, making learning an enjoyable experience for young viewers. The show focuses on a group of puppies led by Bow Wizzle (voiced by Snoop Dogg), who serves as the adult mentor to the rest of the cast, including Woofee (voiced by London), a smooth singer who is always cheering on his friends; Yap Yap, a high-spirited character who is known for her positive and cheery personality; Chow Wow, an empathic team player, and Barks-A-Locks, the curious one of the group who is always discovering new adventures. The show, which has been honored with an NAACP Image Award, Telly Award and Mom’s Choice Award, has amassed 1.3 million subscribers to the Doggyland YouTube channel. Said Snoop Dogg (whose real name is Calvin Broadus Jr.): “Looking back at where we are now with Doggyland and everything, it’s wild. When Cori was just an itty-bitty pup, she was always saying how she wanted to be part of a cartoon, and now here we are. Not only is she a cartoon character, but it’s one she helped create herself. What we’ve got here is a beautiful, full-circle moment, and I’m just so proud to be a part of it as her father. Maxine’s got Cori’s confidence, her personality and a little bit of that secret ingredient. I’m talking about sass. What’s even better is that Maxine is coming in hot with that patented Doggyland positive message. She’s here to let the kids know they should love themselves because you’re already enough just the way you are. Life lesson!” From left: October London, Snoop Dogg and Claude Brooks Chris Enriquez Broadus also is a professional DJ, performing under the moniker of Princess Broadus, and an entrepreneur, working in the worlds of beauty, fashion and music, with a growing focus on building brands and experiences that challenge traditional ideas of identity and culture. The message behind Maxine’s debut in “You’re Enough” is said be at the heart of Doggyland’s mission. Maxine encourages young viewers to embrace their individuality and reminds them that there is nothing they need to change about themselves in order to be worthy, lovable or enough. Maxine’s debut follows on the heels of the introduction of Banjo Bucky, voiced by country music singer Jake Tankersley. Watch the “You’re Enough” music video below. THR

title: DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers
full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:00am PT DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers 1 hour ago Rachel Nichols Will Lead ‘The Story,’ a Daily Show From Sports Illustrated 2 hours ago Disney Broadens Super Bowl LXI Plans With Pat McAfee, Next-Gen Stats 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cheyne Gateley/VIP As media audiences fall apart, one analytics company hopes to knit some of them back together. DataFuelX , a company led by former TV-sales executives is launching DFX Marketplace, a new way for advertisers to connect to commercial inventory across multiple publishers with a single point of entry. The company, co-founded by Dan Aversano and Michael Strober, two sales veterans who have between them logged stints in senior roles at places like WarnerMedia, TelevisaUnivision, and Nexstar Media, among other companies, launches its offer at a moment when advertisers find themselves hard-pressed to reach large groups of consumers across linear or digital. Related Stories 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride “We’re launching a cross-publisher marketplace for linear and CTV, supporting both demographic and audience-based buying. Agencies will have multiple ways to participate –through the platform, APIs or their own AI agents. Our platform will also support direct transaction across linear and digital as well as programmatic execution. This is a very unique model,” says Aversano during a recent email conversation. “Most solutions we have come across are primarily focused on digital-only programmatic transactions.” Popular on Variety The company says DFX Marketplace is supported by 13 premium video publishers representing nearly 40% of linear impressions across more than 50 networks, reaching 70% of U.S. TV households. Aversano declined to name the companies involved, but a Wednesday event unveiling the marketplace is slated to include executives from Fox Corp. and TelevisaUnivison, as well as Sean Cunningham, president and CEO of the VAB, a trade organization that represents most U.S. TV networks to the broader advertising market. The rise of such a marketplace comes as more commercial inventory, particularly that associated with streaming, is purchased in programmatic fashion, or via algorithms and software designed to seek out ad time that is seen by a particular audience niche, such as someone in a particular geographic region, for example, or someone who is likely to be in need of a car or baby products. DataFuelX said its new marketplace will support buying and selling done via agentic AI and will enable AI assistants and customer agents to work across all participating publishers through a single connection. The marketplace is being built to support agentic buying and selling, enabling DFX AI assistants and approved customer agents to work across participating publishers through a single connection while preserving human control over strategy and final decisions. Participants in the new marketplace will be able to keep tabs on planning, activation, optimization and other tasks all under one system. “Premium video remains one of the most powerful ways for advertisers to build reach, but the complexity of differentiating true premium video across an increasingly expanding, but diluted ad inventory infrastructure has limited the growth and its share of overall video ad dollars,” says Cunningham, in a statement. “DFX Marketplace represents an important step toward modernizing that infrastructure for cross-publisher and cross-platform, using intelligence, automation and AI to make premium video easier to access, transact and optimize at scale.” The company says its platform is already used by major publishers and has supported more than $300 million in media transactions. A 20-part true-crime series from Manitoba, Canada-based Black Watch Entertainment has been greenlit, comprising two seasons of 10 episodes shot back-to-back. ITV Studios is attached as the international distributor. Each hourlong episode will reconstruct a murder using a single, grisly clue: a severed limb, torso or other dismembered body part. It follows how investigators race to identify the victim and uncover what happened, using DNA evidence, missing persons reports, digital trails and forensic analysis. Related Stories News How Steven Moffat & Sue Vertue Obsessively Recreated 10 Downing Street For Channel 4's 'Number 10' News ITV Buys 'The Galway Bay Murders' Thriller Starring Kate Mulgrew & Colm Meaney Each story is also told through contributions from investigators, witnesses, family members and experts closest to each case, which is explored from discovery through to justice. Watch on Deadline Missing Pieces qualifies for provincial tax credits of up to 65%, with no Canadian content (CanCon) requirements needed, as Manitoba continues to be a strong option for international productions shooting in Canada. Furthermore, because Black Watch founder Meghan Duffy is the creator, the production also qualifies for a 25% federal tax incentive. “We’re always looking for new ways to tell true-crime stories, and Missing Pieces offers a truly unique perspective,” said Duffy. “Each case starts with a single piece of a victim, and we follow investigators as they work backward to uncover what happened, identify the victim and ultimately find the person responsible.” Duffy is executive producer for Black Watch, with Diana Carter in the same role for Hearst, along with Mark Marabella. Kim Ball is Executive in Charge of Production for Super Channel, and Alison Reid serves as showrunner. Black Watch, founded back in 2010, has credits including Superchannel and ITV’s Finally Caught and Secrets, Lies and DNA Ties ; Lifetime Network’s The Woman With Red Lipstick , I Have to Kill My Neighbor and Match, Meet Murder ; CBC’s Moral Injuries: The Art of Jordan Van Sewell ; and MarVista Entertainment’s Snowmance . Radial Entertainment has teamed with Content Partners and ITV Studios to produce new episodes of the series that examines true crime tales from the perspective of scientific evidence and data analysis. The partners plan to deliver 20 fresh episodes that are expected to spark renewed interest and viewership of the “Forensic Files” library of 400 episodes. The series originated in the mid-1990s on Discovery’s TLC channel as “Medical Detectives.” It’s had numerous incarnations since then and is available on YouTube and other ad-supported streaming platforms. With the new batch of episodes, Radial and Content Partners will give the show a big SEO push across multiple digital platforms. Radial is in the midst of executing the same model on the unrelated unscripted series “The FBI Files.” Related Stories Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. “ ‘Forensic Files’ helped define true crime television, and its focus on science and evidence continues to resonate with one of the most loyal audiences in the genre,” said David Buoymaster, Radial Entertainment’s chief investment officer. “Working with Content Partners to create new episodes is a natural next step in our relationship and an opportunity to build on the series’ legacy.” Popular on Variety Content Partners, the Los Angeles-based rights management firm and holding company, has owned “Forensic Files” since 2024. “From the outset, we saw an opportunity to build on the extraordinary history of ‘Forensic Files,’” said Scott Hemming, Content Partners’ executive VP. “Radial shares our commitment to the series, and with ITV America’s production expertise, we’re excited to bring audiences new investigations with the scientific detail and clarity that have made ‘Forensic Files’ a tentpole of unscripted television.” Buoymaster, Cristina Guggino and Katie Carroll are executive producers for Radial Entertainment, with Steve Kram, Hemming and John Mass serving as executive producers for Content Partners. title: Urban One Lines Up ‘Foul Play’ And ‘Power & Influence’ TikTok Microdramas

Dreux Dougall, who has credits for Lovecraft Country and Tanya Hoffler-Moore ( Tyler Perry’s House of Payne ) are behind of corporate-set thriller Power & Influence and revenge drama Foul Play , respectively. Each series will feature 20 episodes averaging 90 seconds, with Power & Influence debuting on October 19, 2026. Following their exclusive TikTok premieres, they will extend across Urban One’s digital, television, streaming and audio platforms such as on the TV One channel, connect TV sets and free ad-supported channels. Related Stories Acquisitions Sarah Snook & 'Game Of Thrones' Stars Shows Adapted As Microdramas For Snips News 'Night Of The Living Dead' Vertical Microdrama Readied For Horror-Focused App Room418 Power & Influence is currently in production. Logline reads: “AI deepfakes expose hidden scandals at one of Atlanta’s most respected Black-owned advertising agencies, forcing CEO Nia Whitmore to keep her greatest threat close: Zuri Reynolds, a young creative strategist whose street ties could save the company – or destroy everything Nia has built.” Watch on Deadline Cast comprises Ivory Shields ( Nappily Ever After ), Tanazia Madan ( Queen Sugar ), Jay Jones ( Lovecraft Country ), De’Tuan Williams ( Fear Lake Lanier ), Ashley Brittney Silva ( Love & Marriage: DC ) and Donny Carrington ( Beyond the Gates ). The 2026 Rebels With a Cause Competition will screen nine world premieres that explore “unconventional approaches to filmmaking,” organizers of the Estonian fest said on Wednesday. Curated by Javier Garcia Puerto, the program has been celebrating filmmakers who challenge cinematic conventions, bringing together emerging voices and established directors. title: France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Oct 14, 2026 5:16am PT France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) Director Melina León was the first female Peruvian filmmaker to screen at Cannes' Directors' Fortnight with her debut feature 'Song Without a Name,' also handled by Luxbox By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Maeve Jinkings Set for Women’s Convent-Prison Daring Escape Drama ‘Cabildo 71’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Cannes Festival Winning Producer Quijote Films Launches In-House Scripted Series Division (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Portrait Huaco' Credit: Natalia Grande France’s Luxbox and Spain’s Amore Cine have boarded the Peruvian drama “Portrait Huaco” (“Huaco retrato”) by Melina León, best known for her debut feature “Song Without a Name” (“Canción sin nombre”), which world premiered at the 2019 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight. “ After the incredible journey we shared with ‘Song Without a Name,’ I’m thrilled to continue collaborating with Melina, now as both international sales agent and co-producer,” said Luxbox’s Fiorella Moretti. Related Stories Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount She added: “As a Peruvian, it is especially meaningful to help bring Gabriela Wiener’s bold and contemporary work to the screen through Melina’s singular vision. ‘Portrait Huaco’ explores questions at the heart of today’s conversations in a truly original way, and I have no doubt it will resonate with audiences around the world.” Popular on Variety For Paz Lázaro, who co-founded Amore Cine alongside Edson Sidonie (“Karnawal”) and Juan Pablo Felix (“Mil pedazos”), “Adapting Gabriela Wiener’s ‘Portrait Huaco’ means bringing to the screen a work that bridges Latin America and Spain, weaving colonialism, racism, identity and desire with a voice both ancient and radically contemporary.” “For Amore Cine, alongside our fellow producing partners, this is an opportunity to champion a film with international reach that challenges perspectives and reexamines our shared history.” Based on the autobiographical novel of the Peruvian author, the project participates in the 8th Proyecta Co-Production Forum at Ventana Sur , which takes place in Montevideo, Uruguay this year from Nov. 30 – Dec. 4. Amore Cine and Luxbox join Peru’s Mano de Obra Cine, led by Melissa Cordero, and La Vida Misma Films, which produced “Song Without a Name.” The story follows Gabriela who returns to Lima after her father dies. Back home, she discovers a book by her great-great-grandfather, Austrian explorer Charles Wiener. Her search into the family past becomes a reckoning with the lingering legacies of colonialism, internalized racism and abandonment. “’Portrait Huaco’ combines a distinctly Peruvian perspective with universal themes of identity, memory and colonial heritage. Under the direction of Melina León, the film seeks to preserve its cultural roots and Peruvian creative leadership while embracing an international scope through strategic co-production partnerships,” said Cordero. This is the second time for Mano de Obra to co-produce with Amore Cine. Late coming-of-age drama, “Ofelia,” currently in post,’ is a European-Latin American co-production that includes Amore, Argentina’s Bikini Films, Quijote Films of Chile, Brazil’s África Filmes and CUP Filmes, Spain’s Potenza Producciones and France’s Reality Films. Said Cordero: “I’m interested in producing auteur-driven films with a distinctive cinematic voice and strong cultural identity, as well as genre films that can connect with wider audiences. I’m particularly drawn to stories rooted in Peru and Latin America that explore universal themes, bringing local perspectives to an international audience.” “My near-term strategy is to strengthen Mano de Obra Cine’s position as a production company focused on feature films, building strategic co-production partnerships across Latin America and Europe. title: Launch Financing To Expand Short-Term Indie Film Lending On Back Of New $15M Senior Credit Facility
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Berlinale 2027 Retrospective To Explore Visions Of The Future In Nod To Centenary Of Fritz Lang’s ‘Metropolis’ ‘La Bola Negra’, ‘Woman Unknown’, ‘NAZA’ & ‘Fjord’ Among 68 Films On Shortlist For 39th European Film Awards Reese Witherspoon Partners With Mediawan To Buy Hello Sunshine View All October 14, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source André Holland and Kate Mara in 'The Dutchman' Frank DeMarco/Andre Gaines EXCLUSIVE: Beverly Hills-based film finance specialist Launch Financing is poised to scale up its short-term gap loan services for indie productions in the U.S., Canada and the UK having secured its first ever institutional $15M senior credit facility. The film-lending arm of producer-financier Chris K. Daniels’ The Launch Company , has previously funded more than 60 media loans against tax credits, pre-sales and other committed production receivables. Past recipient productions include thriller The Dutchman , black comedy Thumb and coming-of-age comedy The Marshmallow Experiment . Related Stories Casting Eric McCormack Set For Nimisha Mukerji's Psychological Thriller 'You're Safe Now' News 'A Long Winter': Watch First Trailer For Andrew Haigh Drama Starring Fred Hechinger, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Caitríona Balfe & Kit Connor The new $15 million senior credit facility has been provided by specialty lender Pier Asset Management and is Launch Financing’s first institutional warehouse facility. Watch on Deadline The line, extendable to $25 million over time, will enable Launch Financing to scale its short-term production lending to independent films in the U.S., Canada and the UK. “A production’s money always comes slower than the production wants it to. Tax credits, bank closings, equity cashflow and distributor payments arrive on their own schedule, and the schedule is not the shoot’s,” said Daniels. “We built a standardized loan structure that clears diligence in two to five business days and wires within forty-eight hours of signing, because that is the only thing a producer in prep actually needs from a lender. This facility allows us to expand beyond our current pipeline and work more closely with high-quality producers, production companies, agencies and studios, improving the process one film at a time.” Launch Financing advances senior secured capital against money a production is set to receive and is repaid when that money arrives. Loans run eight to twenty-six weeks and are secured in first position against government production incentives, distributor minimum guarantees, pre-sales, committed equity, institutional capital and library-backed corporate guarantees. The money typically covers production cashflow while a bank or institutional lender closes, as well as cast escrow and union deposits, production payroll and finishing funds. Launch Financing sits inside The Launch Company alongside Launch Development, which develops and packages film projects; Cinelaunch, the company’s business-affairs and back-office platform; and Launch North, its physical production operation in Toronto. The lending team has sat on both sides of the table, as producers who have borrowed against tax credits and pre-sales and as the institutional capital that structures those loans. Daniels, who is also a strategic partner at Esme Grace, the boutique firm behind Michael Mann’s Ferrari , serves as chief executive officer of The Launch Company and its lending arm. Wyatt Cavalier is Launch Financing JV’s chief investment officer , and Jess Mastro is head of development for The Launch Company. title: Ben Frow To Leave Skydance’s UK Network 5 After 14 Years
full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Netflix Layoffs Underway, Streamer Eliminating About 1,000 Jobs, 6% Of Its Workforce Read the full story By Jake Kanter , Jesse Whittock , Max Goldbart October 14, 2026 4:14am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Frow Edinburgh TV Festival EXCLUSIVE : The end of an era is approaching at 5 , the UK television network that sits within David Ellison ’s newly minted Skydance empire. Deadline can reveal that Ben Frow will step down as Paramount UK’s chief content officer next year, a role in which he has overseen 5 (formerly Channel 5) for 14 years. A charismatic creative executive, Frow is comfortably 5’s longest-serving content chief, joining in 2012, when British media baron Richard Desmond owned the network. Frow has decided to leave on his own terms, but his anticipated exit comes just a week after Paramount completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, creating the Skydance empire and precipitating a major executive reshuffle. Related Stories News Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance's First Streaming Moves After Merger Close News 'M+/HBO Originals': Movistar Plus & Skydance Extend Partnership Kevin MacLellan, the Paramount international chief who oversaw 5, is exiting the business, as is his Warner Bros. Discovery counterpart Gerhard Zeiler. JB Perrette, one of the big winners of the $110 billion merger, will take on streaming and networks outside of the U.S ., with CBS chief operating officer Bryon Rubin put in temporary charge of 5 and Australia’s Network Ten. Watch on Deadline In an internal email seen by Deadline, 5 president Reemah Sakaan said Frow would step down from his day-to-day role in the summer of 2027. He will remain employed by Skydance until the end of next year. “His exceptional creative skills, obsession with our audience and fiery competitive spirit has led an acclaimed creative transformation of the network and has overseen a phenomenal range of hits,” Sakaan said. “I have only worked with Ben for a short while this year, but it has been an utter joy, so I have some sense of just how much he will be missed.” In the internal email, Frow added: “I have always said that this was the best job in the world, and I’ve absolutely loved my time at 5. But after 14 years where I’ve achieved everything I wanted to and more, it seems like the right time to hand over and give someone else a go. This isn’t a goodbye just yet and I’ll be around to support Reemah and the team with a smooth transition.” During his tenure, Frow has revitalized 5, transforming it from a broadcaster that was largely associated with overseas acquisitions like CSI to become a fleet-footed and risk-taking creative force. Frow’s legacy will perhaps be defined by his decision to cancel Big Brother in 2018. He took the cash from the Banijay-owned reality series and reinvested it into drama and high-end factual content. This gave rise to one of Frow’s biggest hits: All Creatures Great and Small , the Playground-produced drama based on the early career of veterinary surgeon James Herriot. All Creatures , which is co-produced by PBS Masterpiece, consistently delivers big audiences and was the most-watched scripted series on 5’s streaming platform last year. Other hit dramas have included Power: The Downfall of Huw Edwards and The Teacher . In factual, Frow has welcomed big names to the network like Monty Python star Michael Palin, who has journeyed to North Korea and the Philippines for documentary series. 5 scooped BAFTA and Royal Television Society awards in 2024 for White Nanny, Black Child , while Suicidal: In Our Own Words won a Grierson. The network was named Channel of the Year at the Edinburgh TV Festival in 2025, and posted a record operating profit of £71.7 million ($95M) in 2021 . Frow has many admirers in the UK television industry. He is respected by producers for his creative instinct and quick decision-making, while he inspires fierce loyalty among his small team of commissioners. He is an entertaining presence on public platforms: Honest, direct, quick-witted, and unafraid to have a dig at 5’s closest competitors . His mischievous twinkle saw him attend meetings this year wearing a Make Paramount Great Again hat — including during a sit-down with Ellison himself. On stage at the Edinburgh TV Festival in 2023, Frow revealed that he secretly resigned in April 2022 as a result of burnout following the pandemic, saying he felt as if he were being “pecked” alive. He later reversed his decision after his mental health improved. title: Stephen Chow’s ‘Shaolin Soccer’ Spinoff ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China’s Summer Box Office
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Kung Fu Soccer' Encore Films Stephen Chow ’s Kung Fu Soccer is heading to North American and British cinemas after finishing the summer as China’s biggest box office hit. Singapore-based distributor Encore Films said Wednesday that the comedy legend’s long-awaited Shaolin Soccer spinoff will open Oct. 23 in the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Ireland. The rollout will include the original-language version and a newly produced English dub featuring voice performances by Chow, Jimmy O. Yang and MC Jin. The release arrives in the 25th anniversary year of Shaolin Soccer , which became Hong Kong’s highest-grossing local film upon its 2001 release before developing a global cult following. Chow followed it with Kung Fu Hustle (2004), another genre-blending smash that earned more than $100 million worldwide and cemented his reputation as one of Hong Kong’s greatest comedy-action hitmakers. Related Stories Movies Tallinn Black Nights Fest Unveils Baltic Film Competition TV Mikael Marcimain's 'The Cold Song' Marks a Rare Return to Big Swing European TV Drama (Exclusive First Look) Timed at home to tap into this summer’s World Cup fever, Kung Fu Soccer earned approximately $344.4 million (RMB 2.315 billion) during China’s June 1-Aug. 31 summer moviegoing season, becoming the season’s biggest earner. Chow’s return helped lift the country’s summer theatrical revenue to $1.86 billion (RMB 12.498 billion), up 4.45 percent from a year earlier, according to figures from the China Film Administration and Maoyan Research Institute. Written and directed by Chow, Kung Fu Soccer marks his first feature behind the camera since 2019’s The New King of Comedy. Previously announced under the title Shaolin Women’s Soccer , the Hong Kong-China co-production reworks the original film’s martial-arts-meets-scrappy-sports-team premise around an all-female squad of underdogs. ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Encore Films Zhang Xiaofei, the star of Chinese blockbuster Hi, Mom , plays the captain of the Emei Women’s Football Team, which enters the Supreme Invincible Cup determined to prove its doubters wrong. Dilraba Dilmurat plays the team’s star striker, while Lay Zhang serves as its kung fu mentor, helping the players combine martial arts mastery with soccer skills to overcome formidable opponents and setbacks on and off the field. The ensemble also includes Hong Kong screen icon Carina Lau, Japanese star Takeru Satoh, Sisley Choi, Louis Cheung, Yang and Jin. Encore acquired worldwide distribution rights outside mainland China from Chow’s production banner, The Star Overseas , in June. The October openings in the West follow the film’s earlier theatrical rollout across the Asia -Pacific region. “Following the tremendous response to Kung Fu Soccer across Asia and Oceania, we’re excited to bring the film to cinema audiences in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Ireland,” said Encore Films managing director Joyce Lee. “Stephen Chow’s films have always transcended language and cultural boundaries, bringing audiences together through his unique blend of action, comedy and heart,” she added. Encore has also completed a Cantonese dub. “Through a special English-dubbed version that makes the film more accessible to wider audiences, alongside a newly completed Cantonese-dubbed version whose voice cast will be announced soon, we hope to introduce Stephen Chow’s signature style of comedy to new audiences while reconnecting with longtime fans,” Lee said.
